---

Feature: Versioned jarvis-serve-nats.service unit file (FEAT-PO-001)
  As an operator of the jarvis box
  I want the real Slack ingress unit versioned at ops/systemd/jarvis-serve-nats.service
  So that the actual door service is reproducible and no longer confused with the langgraph dev frontdoor

  Background:
    Given the repository has an ops/systemd/ tree
    And the running Slack door is the jarvis-serve-nats user unit

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core artifact — the correct unit file must exist and be identifiable
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The versioned unit file exists in the ops tree
    Given an operator checks out the repository
    When they inspect ops/systemd/
    Then a unit file named jarvis-serve-nats.service should be present

  # Why: The file must unambiguously identify itself as the Slack door
  @key-example
  Scenario: The unit file identifies jarvis-serve-nats as the Slack ingress door
    Given the versioned jarvis-serve-nats.service unit file
    When its metadata is read
    Then the description should name the Slack door as served by jarvis-serve-nats

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Just-inside boundary — a user unit must declare the user-session target
  @boundary
  Scenario: The unit file installs as a systemd user unit
    Given the versioned unit file
    When the install section is read
    Then WantedBy should reference the default user target

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Regression guard — the unit must not resurrect the wrong door definition
  @negative @regression
  Scenario: The versioned unit file is not the langgraph dev frontdoor
    Given the versioned jarvis-serve-nats.service unit file
    When it is compared with the previous jarvis-frontdoor.service definition
    Then it should not reference the langgraph development service

━━ GROUP D: Edge Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: The versioned file must reflect the live configuration, not a stale snapshot
  @edge-case
  Scenario: The versioned unit file matches the running service definition
    Given a running jarvis-serve-nats user unit
    When the versioned unit file is compared with the active unit
    Then its ExecStart and environment should match what is currently running

Feature: Coordinator install step and README (FEAT-PO-002)
  As an operator
  I want a coordinator install step that deploys the versioned unit file
  So that the Slack door is installed consistently across boxes, following the jarvis-frontdoor README pattern

  Background:
    Given a coordinator context with access to the target system

  # Why: Core install path — the unit file must land in the user systemd directory
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The install step deploys the unit file to the user systemd directory
    Given a coordinator with install permissions
    When the install step runs for jarvis-serve-nats.service
    Then the unit file should be copied to the systemd user unit directory
    And a systemd daemon reload should be performed

  # Why: Documentation is part of the deliverable, mirroring the frontdoor README pattern
  @key-example
  Scenario: The README documents the install process
    Given the ops/systemd README
    When I read the install section
    Then it should describe installing jarvis-serve-nats.service
    And it should follow the same structure as the existing jarvis-frontdoor README

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Just-inside — install should carry through to an active, enabled unit
  @boundary
  Scenario: The install step enables and starts the door unit
    Given the unit file has been copied to the user systemd directory
    When the install step finishes
    Then the jarvis-serve-nats unit should be enabled and started

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Guard against partial installs when the artifact is missing
  @negative
  Scenario: The install step fails cleanly when the unit file is missing
    Given ops/systemd/jarvis-serve-nats.service is absent
    When the coordinator install step runs
    Then it should report a clear error and abort without side effects

Feature: Journalctl-based staleness detection (FEAT-PO-003)
  As an on-call operator
  I want a watchdog that reads journalctl --user -u jarvis-serve-nats
  So that socket/subscription staleness is detected when the Slack door goes quiet

  Background:
    Given a journal for the jarvis-serve-nats user unit

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core mechanism — the watchdog must read the right journal source
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The watchdog reads the serve-nats user journal
    Given the watchdog is running
    When it performs a staleness check
    Then it should execute journalctl for the jarvis-serve-nats user unit

  # Why: Healthy path — recent subscription activity must be recognised as alive
  @key-example
  Scenario: The watchdog reports the door alive when subscription activity is recent
    Given the journal contains subscription activity within the quiet window
    When the watchdog checks for staleness
    Then the door should be reported as alive

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Just-outside — the first gap beyond the quiet window must trip the alarm
  @boundary @negative
  Scenario: The watchdog flags staleness when the quiet window is exceeded
    Given the journal shows no subscription activity for longer than the quiet window
    When the watchdog checks for staleness
    Then the door should be reported as stale

  # Why: Just-inside — activity at the window edge must not trigger a false alarm
  @boundary
  Scenario: The watchdog accepts activity at the quiet window boundary
    Given the journal shows subscription activity exactly at the quiet window limit
    When the watchdog checks for staleness
    Then the door should not be reported as stale

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Empty journals are ambiguous — must not false-alarm on fresh boots
  @negative
  Scenario: The watchdog reports an indeterminate state when the journal has no entries
    Given journalctl returns no entries for the unit
    When the watchdog checks for staleness
    Then it should record an indeterminate state without posting a staleness alert

━━ GROUP D: Edge Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: journalctl failure must not be mistaken for a dead subscription
  @edge-case
  Scenario: The watchdog handles a journalctl failure gracefully
    Given journalctl exits with a non-zero status
    When the watchdog runs a staleness check
    Then it should record an error
    And it should not post a false staleness alert

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Feature: Slack alert notification (FEAT-PO-004)
  As an on-call operator
  I want the watchdog to post a Slack alert when the door goes quiet
  So that the absent-operator failure is surfaced instead of silently persisting

  Background:
    Given a watchdog that has detected socket/subscription staleness

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core notification — staleness must produce an operator-visible alert
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: Staleness detection posts a Slack alert
    Given the door has been reported stale
    When the watchdog posts the alert
    Then a Slack message should be sent identifying the jarvis-serve-nats door as stale

  # Why: The command must stay silent when the door is healthy
  @key-example @regression
  Scenario: No Slack alert is posted when the door is alive
    Given the door is reported alive
    When the watchdog completes its check
    Then no Slack alert should be posted

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Delivery failure must be recorded, not swallowed
  @negative
  Scenario: The watchdog records a delivery failure when Slack is unreachable
    Given the Slack endpoint is unavailable
    When the watchdog attempts to post the staleness alert
    Then the delivery failure should be recorded
    And the alert should be retried on the next check

━━ GROUP D: Edge Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Extended quiet must alert once, not every check interval
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Consecutive stale checks do not produce duplicate alerts
    Given a staleness alert was already posted on the previous check
    When the door remains stale on the current check
    Then no new Slack alert should be posted

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Feature: O-30 register correction (FEAT-PO-005)
  As an operator

  Background:

  Scenario: The O-30 register names serve-nats as the Slack door

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: The correction must be surgical — untouched fields remain intact
  @boundary
  Scenario: The register row preserves all other fields
    Given the Slack door row previously named langgraph dev
    When the correction to serve-nats is applied
    Then every other field in the row should be unchanged

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Regression guard — the wrong door must not reappear
  @negative @regression
  Scenario: langgraph dev no longer appears as the Slack door in the register
    When I scan the O-30 register for the Slack door entry
    Then langgraph dev should not be named as the door

FEATURE SPEC PROPOSAL: Jarvis Serve-NATS Watchdog
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Five features within one scope boundary (ops files + watchdog script only, no compose deploy, jarvis is not a DCL venue). Each Feature block is tagged with its FEAT-PO ID for tracking.

---

Feature: Versioned jarvis-serve-nats.service unit file (FEAT-PO-001)
  As an operator of the jarvis box
  I want the real Slack ingress unit versioned at ops/systemd/jarvis-serve-nats.service
  So that the actual door service is reproducible and no longer confused with the langgraph dev frontdoor

  Background:
    Given the repository has an ops/systemd/ tree
    And the running Slack door is the jarvis-serve-nats user unit

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core artifact — the correct unit file must exist and be identifiable
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The versioned unit file exists in the ops tree
    Given an operator checks out the repository
    When they inspect ops/systemd/
    Then a unit file named jarvis-serve-nats.service should be present

  # Why: The file must unambiguously identify itself as the Slack door
  @key-example
  Scenario: The unit file identifies jarvis-serve-nats as the Slack ingress door
    Given the versioned jarvis-serve-nats.service unit file
    When its metadata is read
    Then the description should name the Slack door as served by jarvis-serve-nats

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Just-inside boundary — a user unit must declare the user-session target
  @boundary
  Scenario: The unit file installs as a systemd user unit
    Given the versioned unit file
    When the install section is read
    Then WantedBy should reference the default user target

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Regression guard — the unit must not resurrect the wrong door definition
  @negative @regression
  Scenario: The versioned unit file is not the langgraph dev frontdoor
    Given the versioned jarvis-serve-nats.service unit file
    When it is compared with the previous jarvis-frontdoor.service definition
    Then it should not reference the langgraph development service

━━ GROUP D: Edge Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: The versioned file must reflect the live configuration, not a stale snapshot
  @edge-case
  Scenario: The versioned unit file matches the running service definition
    Given a running jarvis-serve-nats user unit
    When the versioned unit file is compared with the active unit
    Then its ExecStart and environment should match what is currently running

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Feature: Coordinator install step and README (FEAT-PO-002)
  As an operator
  I want a coordinator install step that deploys the versioned unit file
  So that the Slack door is installed consistently across boxes, following the jarvis-frontdoor README pattern

  Background:
    Given a coordinator context with access to the target system

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core install path — the unit file must land in the user systemd directory
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The install step deploys the unit file to the user systemd directory
    Given a coordinator with install permissions
    When the install step runs for jarvis-serve-nats.service
    Then the unit file should be copied to the systemd user unit directory
    And a systemd daemon reload should be performed

  # Why: Documentation is part of the deliverable, mirroring the frontdoor README pattern
  @key-example
  Scenario: The README documents the install process
    Given the ops/systemd README
    When I read the install section
    Then it should describe installing jarvis-serve-nats.service
    And it should follow the same structure as the existing jarvis-frontdoor README

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Just-inside — install should carry through to an active, enabled unit
  @boundary
  Scenario: The install step enables and starts the door unit
    Given the unit file has been copied to the user systemd directory
    When the install step finishes
    Then the jarvis-serve-nats unit should be enabled and started

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Guard against partial installs when the artifact is missing
  @negative
  Scenario: The install step fails cleanly when the unit file is missing
    Given ops/systemd/jarvis-serve-nats.service is absent
    When the coordinator install step runs
    Then it should report a clear error and abort without side effects

Feature: Journalctl-based staleness detection (FEAT-PO-003)
  As an on-call operator
  I want a watchdog that reads journalctl --user -u jarvis-serve-nats
  So that socket/subscription staleness is detected when the Slack door goes quiet

  Background:
    Given a journal for the jarvis-serve-nats user unit

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core mechanism — the watchdog must read the right journal source
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The watchdog reads the serve-nats user journal
    Given the watchdog is running
    When it performs a staleness check
    Then it should execute journalctl for the jarvis-serve-nats user unit

  # Why: Healthy path — recent subscription activity must be recognised as alive
  @key-example
  Scenario: The watchdog reports the door alive when subscription activity is recent
    Given the journal contains subscription activity within the quiet window
    When the watchdog checks for staleness
    Then the door should be reported as alive

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Just-outside — the first gap beyond the quiet window must trip the alarm
  @boundary @negative
  Scenario: The watchdog flags staleness when the quiet window is exceeded
    Given the journal shows no subscription activity for longer than the quiet window
    When the watchdog checks for staleness
    Then the door should be reported as stale

  # Why: Just-inside — activity at the window edge must not trigger a false alarm
  @boundary
  Scenario: The watchdog accepts activity at the quiet window boundary
    Given the journal shows subscription activity exactly at the quiet window limit
    When the watchdog checks for staleness
    Then the door should not be reported as stale

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Empty journals are ambiguous — must not false-alarm on fresh boots
  @negative
  Scenario: The watchdog reports an indeterminate state when the journal has no entries
    Given journalctl returns no entries for the unit
    When the watchdog checks for staleness
    Then it should record an indeterminate state without posting a staleness alert

━━ GROUP D: Edge Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: journalctl failure must not be mistaken for a dead subscription
  @edge-case
  Scenario: The watchdog handles a journalctl failure gracefully
    Given journalctl exits with a non-zero status
    When the watchdog runs a staleness check
    Then it should record an error
    And it should not post a false staleness alert

Feature: Slack alert notification (FEAT-PO-004)
  As an on-call operator
  I want the watchdog to post a Slack alert when the door goes quiet
  So that the absent-operator failure is surfaced instead of silently persisting

  Background:
    Given a watchdog that has detected socket/subscription staleness

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core notification — staleness must produce an operator-visible alert
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: Staleness detection posts a Slack alert
    Given the door has been reported stale
    When the watchdog posts the alert
    Then a Slack message should be sent identifying the jarvis-serve-nats door as stale

  # Why: The command must stay silent when the door is healthy
  @key-example @regression
  Scenario: No Slack alert is posted when the door is alive
    Given the door is reported alive
    When the watchdog completes its check
    Then no Slack alert should be posted

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Delivery failure must be recorded, not swallowed
  @negative
  Scenario: The watchdog records a delivery failure when Slack is unreachable
    Given the Slack endpoint is unavailable
    When the watchdog attempts to post the staleness alert
    Then the delivery failure should be recorded
    And the alert should be retried on the next check

━━ GROUP D: Edge Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Extended quiet must alert once, not every check interval
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Consecutive stale checks do not produce duplicate alerts
    Given a staleness alert was already posted on the previous check
    When the door remains stale on the current check
    Then no new Slack alert should be posted

Feature: O-30 register correction (FEAT-PO-005)
  As an operator
  I want the O-30 register to name serve-nats as the Slack door
  So that operational documentation matches the real ingress service

  Background:
    Given the O-30 register exists in the operational docs

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Core correction — the register must identify the real door
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: The O-30 register names serve-nats as the Slack door
    Given the O-30 register
    When I read the Slack door row
    Then the service should be named jarvis-serve-nats

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: The correction must be surgical — untouched fields remain intact
  @boundary
  Scenario: The register row preserves all other fields
    Given the Slack door row previously named langgraph dev
    When the correction to serve-nats is applied
    Then every other field in the row should be unchanged

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (1 scenario) ━━

  # Why: Regression guard — the wrong door must not reappear
  @negative @regression
  Scenario: langgraph dev no longer appears as the Slack door in the register
    When I scan the O-30 register for the Slack door entry
    Then langgraph dev should not be named as the door
